title: 3D Rendering in Milan: Furniture, Product, Interiors | 22 Signals
description: 3D rendering in Milan for furniture and design brands, product makers and developers: photoreal CGI of every finish, ready for catalogues, sites and Salone.
h1: 3D rendering in Milan for design brands with more finishes than a studio can shoot
intro: We create photoreal 3D rendering for Milan furniture and design brands, product manufacturers, packaging teams and property developers. From CAD files, drawings or samples we build accurate models, then render every finish, colour and setting you need for catalogues, websites, dealers and press, without booking a photo studio for each new variant.

p: A single armchair from a Brianza manufacturer might come in four frame finishes, two leg styles and sixty fabrics and leathers. That is hundreds of combinations. Photographing them all is impossible, so most brands shoot a handful and leave dealers and customers to imagine the rest. Orders suffer, and so do returns.

3D rendering solves this. Once the chair is modelled accurately and each material is built properly, any combination can be rendered on demand, in any room setting, at any angle. That is why so much of the furniture imagery in Milan catalogues today is CGI, even when nobody can tell.

sections.h: Why CGI often beats a photo shoot
p: A traditional shoot for a new collection means shipping prototypes to a studio, hiring a set designer, a photographer and stylists, and hoping the light on the day is right. If a fabric changes after the shoot, or the marketing team wants a different room, the whole process starts again. Prototypes also get damaged in transit, and some pieces are simply too large or too heavy to move easily.

With rendering, the set is digital. Camera angles, light, season and styling can change late without anyone travelling. A brand can show the same sofa in a Milan apartment, a Swiss chalet and a Dubai villa, each suited to the market it is sold in. Photography still has its place, especially for lifestyle and people, and many brands now mix the two. We help decide which images to shoot and which to render, so the budget goes where it makes the most difference.

sections.h: Images for dealers, specifiers and press
p: Different audiences need different files. Dealers want consistent cut-outs on white for their own sites and price lists. Architects and interior designers want high-resolution details and mood images they can put into presentations. Journalists preparing a design week round-up want a small set of strong images with clear credits. We plan the shot list around all of them, name and organise the files properly, and deliver them in a structure your team can share without confusion.

sections.h: Salone del Mobile and the collection calendar
p: Every April, Salone del Mobile at Fiera Milano Rho sets the year for the design industry. New collections are often still prototypes weeks before the fair, yet catalogues, press kits and dealer material need images now. Rendering lets marketing work in parallel with production. Images are made from the CAD files while the first pieces are still being made, and updated if the design changes.
After the fair, the same models produce the rest of the range in every finish, the room sets for the website and the visuals for social media. One model, many uses, across the whole season.

For design brands, a render that flatters the product is a liability. A walnut that looks too warm or a velvet that looks too shiny leads to disappointed customers and returns. We work from your physical samples, colour references and technical drawings, and we check renders against them before they are approved. Materials are built once and kept in a library, so the same oak looks the same across every product and every year.

Milan has seen a long run of new residential and office developments, from Porta Nuova and CityLife to the regeneration of former rail yards and industrial sites. Developers and agents need to sell apartments long before they exist. Interior designers need to show clients a scheme before they order anything.

We produce exterior and interior visuals from architectural drawings, with materials, furniture and light that suit Milan's buildings and the expectations of its buyers. Images can be adjusted as the specification changes, and interiors can be furnished with your chosen brands' products where they supply 3D files.

sections.h: From model to finished image: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
list: Talk: a 15-minute call about the products, the images you need and the deadline.
Plan: we review your files and samples, and send a written shot list, schedule and cost in 5 to 7 days.
Build: modelling, materials, lighting and rendering, with review rounds and dates in writing.
Grow: new finishes, settings and formats as the range grows, from the same models.

p: Every model we build belongs to you and is delivered in formats that work beyond the first project. The same files can feed an online configurator, an augmented reality view on the product page, an animation for a launch film or the 3D downloads that architects and specifiers ask for. Because our team also builds websites and produces video, those next steps can happen without starting again.

sections.h: How reviews and samples work for a Milan brand
p: Rendering rarely needs everyone in one room. Files arrive securely online, samples are posted, and reviews happen on shared boards where you mark up each image. Calls are booked at times that suit your Milan team. For complex material work we sometimes visit the showroom or factory to see finishes in person, and we plan that into the schedule when it is needed.
Our team delivers in English. Captions, catalogue text and labels in Italian can be arranged with native partners if you need them as part of the same job.

faqs.q: What does 3D rendering in Milan cost?
faqs.a: It depends on how many products, finishes and room sets you need. Once a product is modelled, extra finishes cost much less than the first image. We price after reviewing your files and send a written quote.

faqs.q: Will renders look real enough for a luxury catalogue?
faqs.a: Yes, when the models and materials are built carefully from real samples. Much high-end furniture imagery is already CGI. We check every render against your samples before approval.

faqs.q: Can you work from our CAD files?
faqs.a: Yes. CAD files are the best starting point. If you only have drawings, photos or physical samples, we model from those instead.

faqs.q: Can you deliver images in time for Salone del Mobile?
faqs.a: If we start early enough, yes. We plan backwards from the fair and confirm in writing what can be delivered by each date.
You do. Models, materials and final images are delivered to you and can be reused for configurators, AR, animation and future campaigns.

faqs.q: Do you render architecture and interiors as well as products?
faqs.a: Yes. We produce exterior and interior visuals for developers, agents, architects and interior designers, from drawings and specifications.
